findings.finding: The AC 'Local, GHA-shaped, Jenkins-shaped, GitLab-shaped, and bare invocations share pause behavior' and the bare-remote canonical-sync AC are not tied to a named plan step or a clearly assigned test file; the plan steps name generic 'focused new fsck/doctor repair ownership tests' and a 'two-clone contention regression' but do not name a step that produces the five-provider-shaped invocation matrix.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'Local, GHA-shaped, Jenkins-shaped, GitLab-shaped, and bare invocations share pause behavior.' / Plan steps 2-4

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document an expand-contract/rollback for removing gh workflow-disable and add an AC confirming GHA-triggered canonical sync is blocked by the pause ref (not only the bare-remote path).
evidence: 'This keeps the currently working GitHub safety behavior while also covering local, Jenkins, GitLab, and bare environments'
No rollback/back-out or expand-contract sequencing is stated for removing the existing gh-based safety
findings.finding: Removing `gh workflow disable/enable` is a behavior change to a working safety mechanism, but the plan provides no rollback/back-out path and no explicit confirmation that the replacement mechanism (a durable pause ref honored by the reconciler) prevents the same effect the workflow-disable achieved in GHA (e.g. preventing scheduled/triggered workflows from running canonical sync during repair). The plan asserts equivalence ('keeps the currently working GitHub safety behavior') without an expand-contract or reversibility mechanism.
findings.location: Context: 'Remove the GitHub CLI workflow-disable/enable dependency' / step 6
scenarios: A GHA-scheduled reconcile fires during repair and, because workflows are no longer disabled, races the paused bridge if the reconciler does not honor the pause ref in the GHA path
findings.suggested_fix: Add a back-out note (retain gh disable behind a flag until the pause-ref path is proven) or an AC that a GHA-shaped triggered sync observes the durable pause and refuses to run, closing the equivalence gap.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the operator-facing diagnostic (message/log) emitted when cleanup fails and leaves the durable pause for manual recovery.
evidence: AC: 'A cleanup CAS miss is surfaced without retrying against a new OID.'
AC: 'A cleanup failure leaves the durable pause for operator recovery.'
Only the missing-identity error string is specified verbatim; cleanup-failure operator messaging is not
findings.finding: The cleanup-failure paths ('A missing pause during cleanup returns nonzero without recreating it', 'A cleanup CAS miss is surfaced without retrying', 'A cleanup failure leaves the durable pause for operator recovery') specify fail-closed semantics but do not specify the operator-facing signal — the exit behavior beyond 'nonzero' and any diagnostic message/log that tells the operator a pause was left for manual recovery.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: cleanup ACs / repair sequence step 6
scenarios: Cleanup CAS misses; operator sees a nonzero exit but no message indicating a durable pause remains and requires manual recovery
findings.suggested_fix: Add a stated surface message (e.g. 'Error: <surface> repair left refs/reconciler/gate paused; clear it manually after verifying state') and cover it with the cleanup-failure test.

findings.checklist_item: Correct the Context to state that the GitHub-only `gh workflow disable/enable` pause exists ONLY in fsck_repair.py and that `doctor --repair` currently has no pause (only the shared in-flight lock abort), so its work is ADDING repair-owned pause ownership rather than replacing a gh dependency.
evidence: fsck_repair.py:286 `subprocess.run(["gh", "workflow", "disable", "reconcile-bridge.yml"]...)` — the gh pause exists only in fsck
search_files for 'gh workflow' in doctor.py returned (no matches); search for 'pause'/'_reconciler_pause' in doctor.py returned (no matches)
doctor.py:226 run_repair guards only via `_reconciler_in_flight(repo_root)` (the provider-neutral lock probe), then _pre_tag + repair_finding — no pause acquire/clear at all
This makes 'replace the gh pause on doctor' a false premise: doctor has no pause to replace, so step 6 (removing gh dependency) and the 'GitHub-only' framing do not describe doctor's current state
findings.finding: The Context asserts GitHub-only 'gh workflow disable/enable' safety exists 'around destructive repair', but doctor.py's repair path has no gh workflow calls and no pause mechanism at all -- only the shared provider-neutral _reconciler_in_flight lock probe. The gh-based pause (_reconciler_pause/_reconciler_resume) exists ONLY in fsck_repair.py.
findings.location: Context, para 1 ('Replace GitHub-only `gh workflow disable/enable` safety around destructive repair'); doctor.py run_repair (lines 222-244); fsck_repair.py _reconciler_pause/_reconciler_resume (lines 281-296)
scenarios: Implementer reads the Context, looks for gh workflow disable/enable in doctor.py to remove, and finds nothing -- confusion about whether the surface was already migrated or whether they must ADD (not replace) a pause on doctor
Reviewer of the resulting change cannot map 'removed the GitHub dependency from doctor' to any pre-existing doctor code
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the Context to: 'Replace fsck's GitHub-only `gh workflow disable/enable` pause and ADD the same durable, provider-neutral pause ownership to `doctor --repair`, which today guards destructive repair only with the shared in-flight `refs/reconciler/lock` abort and has no pause of its own.'
